page: Amazon Web Services m8i-flex.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 64 virtual CPUs across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading, running at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The processor is equipped with a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It includes 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance utilizes the Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores placing in the top 25 percent. The hardware supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions, which contribute to top-tier performance in image processing and large language model prompt processing for 70B models. Memory read bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 5112.66 GB/sec for cached blocks and 197.6 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Static web serving throughput is also exceptional, registering in the top 10 percent at 105.74 GB/sec.

The m8i-flex.16xlarge offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads requiring high compute density and memory speed without the added expense of local NVMe storage or GPU hardware. However, single-core performance and large-block memory write speeds are moderate, landing in the average tier. Network bandwidth is limited to a 15 Gbps baseline. This instance is highly suited for database operations, static web serving, software compilation, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
